definitions.explanation: A place where craftspeople, artisans, or artists create their works. Implies hands-on creative or skilled work, often on a small scale.

examples.japanese: {陶芸|とうげい}{工房|こうぼう}を{見学|けんがく}する。
この{工房|こうぼう}では{手作|てづく}りのガラス{製品|せいひん}を{作|つく}っている。
examples.english: At this workshop, they make handmade glass products.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{古|ふる}い{倉庫|そうこ}を{改装|かいそう}して{自分|じぶん}の{工房|こうぼう}にし、そこで{毎日|まいにち}{家具|かぐ}を{作|つく}っている。
examples.english: He renovated an old warehouse into his own workshop and makes furniture there every day.

notes:
STRUCTURE:
{工|こう} (work, craft) + {房|ぼう} (room, chamber).

USAGE:
{工房|こうぼう} has a craft-oriented nuance, suggesting skilled handwork and artisanal production. It is commonly used for pottery, glasswork, woodworking, leather goods, and similar crafts. Compare with {工場|こうじょう} (factory), which implies larger-scale industrial production. Many {工房|こうぼう} are open to visitors and offer hands-on experiences.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {陶芸|とうげい}{工房|こうぼう}: pottery workshop
- ガラス{工房|こうぼう}: glass workshop
- {革|かわ}{工房|こうぼう}: leather workshop
- {工房|こうぼう}{見学|けんがく}: workshop tour
- {工房|こうぼう}を{構|かま}える: to set up a workshop
